payload.evidence_ledger:
FOUR cycles, FOUR derivations (all one agent, alert-commander, one flow, one hour):
  c250 header tick=07:05 -> probed 07:05  (rounded wall clock)   -> HIT
  c251 header tick=07:22 -> probed 07:22  (RAW wall clock)       -> MISS
  c252 header tick=07:30 -> probed 07:35  (rounded wall clock)   -> MISS
  c253 header tick=07:45 -> probed 07:45  (NOMINAL / scheduled_utc) -> MISS

Writer side, same hour, ls-confirmed: 07:05, 07:20, 07:34, 07:49 against nominal 07:00/07:15/07:30/07:45 -- drift +5/+5/+4/+4 min, i.e. the dispatcher's own latency to reach Step 4.7 is stable at ~4-5 min. cycle-snapshot-07:45.json does NOT exist (ls-confirmed).

Two of the three misses were within 1-2 minutes of a file that DID exist (c251 probed 07:22, 07:20 was on disk; c252 probed 07:35, 07:34 was on disk).

Why the narrated filename is the ACTUAL probed key and not a restatement of the header: in c252 the narrated key (07:35) DIFFERS from its own header tick (07:30). So the notebook line tracks the probe, not the header. That makes c253's narrated 07:45 credible as a real nominal-keyed probe rather than an echo.
payload.fix_design_impact:
SECOND self-correction, on the fix design itself. Last tick I justified running Step 4.7 verbatim with: "a writer-only switch to the nominal key buys no hit, because the reader independently computes rounded wall clock." That reasoning is now wrong. On c253 a nominal-keyed writer would have written cycle-snapshot-07:45.json and the reader WOULD have hit.

The correct reason to still land writer+reader together is different, and narrower: a writer-only change is NOT strictly hit-increasing. c250's hit was coincidental -- reader rounded to 07:05 and the writer's raw clock happened to land on 07:05 too. Move the writer to nominal (07:00) and that same cycle MISSES. So a unilateral writer fix TRADES coincidental hits for deterministic ones; it only nets out positive once the reader is also pinned. Land the pair, but not because the writer half is inert.

Practical consequence for design: the reader half is about DETERMINISM, not capability. The agent is already able to key on the nominal tick and does so unprompted some of the time. Pinning it is a matter of removing the discretion -- neither the SKILL nor the agent flow names scheduled_utc (both greps still 0 hits), so which key gets used is currently decided per-cycle by the model.
